Fade from the first shot to the second, hold each picture long enough to read it, and the whole gallery turns into a loop you can send to somebody who was not at the wedding.

tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.two_nu: Two numbers decide how a GIF feels: the width of the file and how long each photo is held. Get them right and the animation looks intentional; get them wrong and it looks like a slideshow that lost the plot.

tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.h2_text.why_g: Why GIF colours look flatter than your photos
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.a_gif_: A GIF holds only 256 colours. That is the format, not a fault in your photographs: the format has carried that limit since CompuServe introduced it in 1987, and every GIF in every chat app today still works the same way. A wedding photo with smooth skin tones, a soft sky or a gradient veil has to be squeezed into a much smaller range, and the result reads as slightly grainy or slightly flat.
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.this_t: This tool builds one shared palette of 256 colours from all your photos together, which is the honest way to do it. Every frame draws from the same set of colours, so the animation does not flicker between frames. The trade-off is that a very warm picture and a very cold picture in the same set have to agree on a middle ground, and one of them can shift a shade. That is the same limitation every ranking GIF maker publishes, and there is no way around it without changing the format.
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.two_pr: Two practical tips. Keep the set to photos shot in the same light - one golden-hour set looks far better than five sets from five different rooms. And if a shot matters more than the others, give it a smaller file by leaving it out of the loop and posting it separately.
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.h2_text.why_s: Why some frames have bars around them
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.a_gif_: A GIF cannot change its size in the middle of an animation, so the canvas is fixed by the first photo you add. If your second photo is a different shape - a tall portrait after a wide group shot - it has to be fitted inside the same frame. That is where the bars come from, and it is the single most common question asked of every free GIF maker, because the tool never explains it.
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.span_text.the: There are only two honest answers, and this tool gives you both.
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.span_text.kee: keeps every pixel and shows the empty space as bars around the picture.
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.span_text.cov: covers the empty space by cropping the photo to the shape of the canvas, which loses a strip of the picture but gives a clean, edge-to-edge animation. For a wedding set that mixes a tall portrait with wide shots, filling the frame usually looks better on a phone, where the bars would otherwise be very obvious.
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.order_: Order helps too. The first photo sets the shape of the whole animation, so put a photo in roughly the same shape as most of your others in first place, and the bars mostly disappear on their own.
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.h2_text.where: Where a wedding GIF works best
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.a_gif_: A GIF is a good fit for a short, still, looping moment - the entrance, the kiss, the first dance, the confetti. It is a poor fit for a long ceremony, because a GIF has no sound and no playback controls.
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.span_text.a_s: A short loop is exactly what these are built for, and a 480 pixel file under a couple of megabytes arrives instantly.
A silent, looping, self-contained file needs no video player and no link - it starts playing where it is posted.

tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.span_text.at_: at the venue or at home. Here a GIF that plays once is often better than one that loops, because a loop at the wrong moment is the thing people notice.

How do I make a GIF from wedding photos?
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.add_yo: Add your photos, choose how they should move into each other - a fade, a slide or a zoom - set how long each photo stays on screen, then build the GIF and download it. The whole thing runs in your browser, so the pictures are never uploaded and the finished file is on your device in a few seconds.
Are my photos uploaded to a server?
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.no_you: No. Your photos are read, resized and animated by your own browser, and the GIF is encoded there as well. Nothing is sent to a server, no account is needed, and there is no watermark on the file.
Which image formats can I use?
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.jpg_pn: JPG, PNG and WebP work everywhere. HEIC files from an iPhone can be converted first with the HEIC to JPG tool on this site, and camera RAW files need to be exported to JPG before any browser can open them.
How many photos can I put in one GIF?
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.up_to_: Up to 20 photos at a time. A published guide for free GIF makers recommends between 3 and 20 images per animation, and more than that makes the file heavy and the waiting longer.
Why do my photos look grainy in the GIF?
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.a_gif_: A GIF holds only 256 colours, so a wedding photo with smooth skin tones or a soft sky has to be squeezed into a much smaller colour range. Everything in this GIF shares one palette of 256 colours chosen from all your photos together, so pictures with very different colours can shift a shade.
Why do some frames have bars around them?
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.the_gi: The GIF canvas takes its shape from your first photo, because a GIF cannot change size in the middle of an animation. A photo with a different shape is either fitted whole, so the empty space shows as bars, or cropped to fill the frame, so the edges of the photo are cut instead. You can switch between the two at any time.
Can I make the GIF loop forever, or play just once?
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.both_l: Both. Loop forever is the default and is what a chat app or a social post expects. Play once writes the file without a loop instruction, so it stops on the last photo - the right choice for a screen or a digital frame.
How do I make the GIF faster or slower?
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.the_sp: The speed control sets how long each photo is held, from 200 milliseconds to 2 seconds. For a calm slideshow of wedding portraits use 800 to 1000 milliseconds per photo. For a quick motion sequence use 200 to 400 milliseconds, which is roughly 10 frames per second.
What size should my wedding GIF be?
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.480_pi: 480 pixels is the safe choice for a chat app or an email, and it is the size a published guide recommends for a small, fast animation. Use 320 pixels for an email signature or a small sticker, and 800 pixels when the file is going on a big screen. Keep the finished file under 5 MB for practical web use.
Is the wedding photo to GIF maker free?
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.yes_th: Yes. There is no account, no watermark, no daily limit and no charge. The GIF is encoded and saved on your own device, and every tool on this site works the same way.
tools.wedding-photo-to-gif.p_text.the_sa: The same photographs become a wedding video with music your guests can actually watch. It runs in the same browser, and nothing is uploaded either.
